sheet-2.description: The waterfront end of Burlington City's business district on the Delaware River, from Stacy Street at the top of the sheet to Wood Street at the bottom, with East and West Union Streets bounding the right edge and the river at the left. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left, so High or Main Street runs straight across the middle and East and West Pearl Streets and the Delaware Avenues run up and down. Above High Street the blocks hold brick stores along the street, Hope Fire Co. No. 1 and Endeavor Fire Co. No. 1, a Presbyterian church with its Sunday school, Granger's Hall, a sewer pipe yard, a laundry, a carriage house and many frame dwellings. Below High Street are the Temple Bnai Israel Synagogue, stores and offices, the Masonic Hall, the Public Library and more dwellings, with a cleared area near the bottom. Along the river lie the City Wharf, a freight shed, storage sheds, the Burlington Supply Co. store house and hardware, Price and Craft coal and lime, a garage, a boat house and a warehouse. The shore is drawn as a stepped line of piers and bulkheads. Blocks are numbered 14 to 19, and the edges of sheets 3, 6 and 17 are outlined but left blank. Water pipes and their sizes are lettered in every street. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: High or Main Street is today's High Street; East and West Pearl are East Pearl Street and West Pearl Street.
The Delaware Avenues along the river are not in the OpenStreetMap street names used here; the nearest modern streets are Riverbank and Pearl Boulevard.
East Union Street lies slightly off the modern line (junction residuals of 4 to 5 m).
Waterfront blocks from Stacy to Wood, E/W Union at right, Delaware River at left; turned, north upper left (rot -71). E/W Delaware Av has no modern match; East Union junctions carry 4-4.5 m.

sheet-3.description: The commercial centre of Burlington City: the two blocks on either side of High (Main) Street between Union Street and Broad Street, from Stacy Street at the top of the sheet to Wood Street at the bottom. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left, so Union and Broad Streets run down the sheet and High Street across it. Both sides of High Street are lined with brick stores, offices, banks and drug stores, most of two and three stories, with dwellings behind them. The block north of High Street holds the City Garage, the J. G. Sholl greenhouses and florist, a Public Service Corporation warehouse, a moving-picture theatre (the Regent Theatre), a candy factory and the Young America Hose Co. No. 3 fire station on East Broad Street. The block south of High Street holds stores at the High Street end, the Friends' Meeting House with its cemetery filling much of the block, the Bell Telephone Co. building on West Broad Street, and rows of brick dwellings along West Union Street, with Ellis Alley and Smith Alley running through the block. Broad Street is drawn about 100 to 112 feet wide with the Pennsylvania Railroad track down its middle. Water pipes and their sizes are marked in every street. The edges of the neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 7 and 17 are outlined but left blank. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Broad Street is drawn 100 to 112 ft wide with the Pennsylvania Railroad in its centre; today's River Line follows the drawn track. The OpenStreetMap and parcel position of Broad Street lies about 8 m off the drawn centre, so the Broad Street junctions were placed from the River Line crossings (High, Wood, and Lawrence Street, which continues Stacy Street east of Broad).
The printed street name High is labelled 'High or Main'; today it is High Street.
Friends' Meeting House and its cemetery occupy the middle of the block south of High Street.

High (Main) Street between Union and Broad, Stacy to Wood; turned, north to the upper left. Broad Street drawn 100-112 ft with the P.R.R. (today's River Line) in its centre: OSM/parcel Broad Street lies about 8 m off the drawn centre, so Broad junctions are taken from River Line crossings. Pilot sheet; detector defaults.

sheet-4.description: The blocks east of Broad Street in the centre of Burlington City, between Lawrence Street at the top of the sheet and Wood Street at the bottom, with Federal Street along the right edge. The sheet is turned like its neighbours, with north towards the upper left, so High or Main Street runs across the middle and East and West Broad Street run down the left side with the Pennsylvania Railroad passenger station and tracks beside them. Along Broad Street stand the Auditorium Theatre and Auditorium Hotel, a garage, the Washington Hotel, the Metropolitan Inn, the Alcazar Hotel, Peter's Garage and the Post Office. Further in are the Moving Picture Theatre, City Hall, an apartment building and a plumber's shop, and a G.A.R. Hall and the J. H. Birch carriage factory near Lawrence Street. The M.E. Church stands at the top left. The upper right of the sheet is occupied by the Methodist Cemetery and scattered dwellings. Locust Avenue divides the large block south of High Street from rows of frame and brick dwellings, with the Moose Club near the bottom left. Block numbers 21, 23 and 73 appear, and the edges of sheets 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 18 are outlined. Water pipe sizes are marked in the streets. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Broad Street is drawn about 100 ft wide with the Pennsylvania Railroad in it; today's River Line follows the track, and the OpenStreetMap Broad Street line lies about 8 m off the drawn centre, so River Line crossings were used instead of Broad Street.
Lawrence, at the top of the sheet, is today's Lawrence Street (the old Stacy east of Broad).
East of Broad: Lawrence (top) to Wood, W/E Federal at right; Broad with the P.R.R. in it (River Line crossings used); turned (rot -70).

sheet-5.description: The southeastern part of the centre of Burlington City, from Lawrence Street at the top to Wood Street at the bottom, between West Federal Street at the left edge and Wall Street at the right. The sheet is turned with north towards the upper left. High or Main Street crosses the middle, with Locust Avenue and Wood Street further down. East Federal Street runs diagonally up to the right from the left edge, lined with rows of frame dwellings, and Wetherill Street crosses it on a diagonal; Lawrence Street bends in two directions at the top. Above High Street are the Robt. Stacy High School, the Ivans Petit Manufacturing canned goods works, a garage and auto sales building, a coloured Baptist church, and the Enterprise Publishing Co. printing and publishing plant, a fire-proof building with a coal bin, at the right edge. Below High Street are All Saints Church, Memorial Hall, the large Wilbur Watts High School with its gymnasium, scattered dwellings and the Burlington Turn Shoe Co. factory near the bottom. Much of the lower right is open ground in blocks 42 and 43, and a large block 285 lies at the top right beside Jackson Street. Water pipes and their sizes are marked in the streets. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Wetherill appears to be today's Belmont Street (the modern street lies along the drawn line); this is inferred from position, not from a name match.
W. Federal is today's West Federal Street; E. Federal is East Federal Street.
Junctions along West Federal Street (Locust Avenue and Wood Street) were placed by hand, because the street is on the edge of the sheet with only one side drawn.

Lawrence/E Federal/Wetherill diagonal blocks and school grounds, W Federal at the left edge to Wall at right; turned (rot -71). Wetherill is today's Belmont Street. Two hand-picked points on W Federal (left edge), corrected by the lead to the street centre at the water pipe.

sheet-6.description: The riverfront blocks of Burlington City north of High Street, from St. Mary Street at the top of the sheet to Stacy Street at the bottom, between the Delaware River at the left and East Union Street at the right. The sheet is turned, with north towards the upper left, so East Pearl Street runs up the middle and Dilwyn, York and Stacy Streets run across. Along the river are the Burlington Water Works with its filter, concrete reservoir, stand pipe, coal bin and suction pipes, the Oneida Boat Club, Jos. Witherow's City Flour Mill with hay storage and a wagon shed, a public boat house and several vacant buildings. East Delaware Avenue runs along the shore with Prior's Alley crossing it. Inland are the Jersey Shoe Co. manufacturing plant at the top, James Latta and Son lumber shed and yard, an A.M.E. Church with a graveyard, the Civil League Club, the Aged Women's Home, the Union M.E. Church, a garage near the bottom and the Y.W.C.A. at the lower right. The rest of the area is dwellings, many of brick, with some stores along York Street. Blocks are numbered 6 to 13, and the edges of sheets 2, 7 and 9 are outlined. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: A narrow strip of water-front land at the left is lettered 'not named'.
The fitted scale is a little smaller (7.55 px/ft) than on neighbouring sheets, and the sheet is turned about 84 degrees against 70 on sheets 2 to 5.
Riverfront north of High: St Mary to Stacy, Delaware River to E Union; turned (rot -84, scale 7.55 px/ft, both consistent with its streets).

sheet-7.description: The area east of Broad Street in the northern part of Burlington City's centre, from East Union Street at the top to Clarkson Street at the bottom, between Stacy and Lawrence Streets on the left and St. Mary Street on the right. North is towards the top of the sheet. East Broad Street crosses the middle with the Pennsylvania Railroad track down its centre, and Barclay Street, York Street and Mechanic Street cross or meet it. The block north of Broad is largely dwellings and small stores along East Union and Barclay Streets, with a First Baptist Church and several vacant buildings at the left, an auto garage and several auto houses at the centre and St. Maria Academy at the upper right. Along Broad Street are rows of brick stores. South of Broad are the Geo. T. Newell heating pad factory, a vacant factory building, Elk Hall, the Public School No. 4, auto sheds, a bakery and dwellings along Lawrence, Laumaster, Mechanic and St. Mary Streets. Stable Alley and Earl's Court run through the northern blocks. Blocks are numbered 24 to 29 and 106 to 107. The edges of sheets 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 are outlined. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Broad Street is drawn about 100 ft wide with the Pennsylvania Railroad in the centre, so River Line crossings (York and Saint Mary Streets) were used instead of Broad Street.
Mechanic Street and Clarkson Street do not agree with the modern OpenStreetMap lines (junction residuals of 3 to 10 m); they were left out of the control.
Barclay is labelled 'Barclay (Earl's Ct)'.

North of Broad: E Union to Clarkson, Stacy/Lawrence to St Mary; north-up (rot +7). Mechanics, Laumaster and Clarkson Streets left out (Clarkson residuals 3-5 m, shifted px/ft 7.68 to 7.50); bottom third without control.

sheet-8.description: The eastern edge of Burlington City's centre, from Clarkson Street at the top to Wetherill and Wall Streets at the bottom, between Lawrence Street at the left and St. Mary Street at the right. North is roughly towards the top of the sheet. York Street runs down the middle, with Jones Avenue and Green Street crossing it. East Federal Street runs diagonally across the lower half, lined on both sides with frame dwellings, and Wetherill Street runs parallel beneath it. A large cemetery fills the upper left, with the Westinghouse Electric Co. office and works, an auto house and a fire station at its lower edge. Long rows of dwellings face York Street, with a garage for 18 cars, a plumbing shop, a junk yard and further dwellings on the blocks east of York Street. At the York and East Federal junction stand Van Sciver's Hotel, an A. J. Jordan wheelwright shop and an auto painting shop. Blocks are numbered 35 to 40, and the edges of sheets 4, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 21 are outlined. Water pipes are lettered in the streets. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Wetherill appears to be today's Belmont Street (inferred from position).
The East Federal / York junction could not be placed reliably; York Street bends there.
York St corridor, Clarkson to Wetherill/Wall, Lawrence to St Mary; north-up (rot +10). Wetherill is today's Belmont Street. Bottom half without control.

sheet-9.description: The north end of Burlington City between the Delaware River and the Assiscunk Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the left of the page. East Pearl, Penn, East Union and Barclay Streets run across the sheet from the river side, crossed by Tatham Street near the top and by Saint Mary Street at the bottom, with the blocks of sheets 6, 7 and 10 outlined beyond. The two lower blocks between East Pearl and East Union Streets hold frame and brick dwellings of two and two and a half stories, with a bakery, a vacant lot and a few stables; solid rows of brick dwellings fill the blocks along Barclay Street. On the river side of East Pearl Street stand a hotel with saloon, the Lakanoo Boat Club, an old men's club, a hay and feed store and the coal and lumber yard of H. H. Carwood, and at the bottom left the Burlington Alcohol Distilling Co., a large brick works with warehouse, engine room and chemical house. North of Tatham Street lie the Neidich Cellustra Co. (artificial horsehair), the lumber yards and mill of J. T. Severn's Sons and Co. Inc. with long lumber sheds, an auto-repair garage and auto houses, and the water edge of the Assiscunk Creek and the Delaware River, here cut by a bridge crossing the creek mouth. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches are shown in the streets. Fire alarm boxes and test hydrants are marked.
notes: Barclay, Tatham, Penn, East Union and East Pearl Streets keep their names today; Saint Mary is Saint Mary Street in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is turned: north is towards the left of the page (rotation about -89 degrees).
East Pearl Street and Saint Mary Street at the bottom edge could not be detected; the bottom row is a boundary of the sheet.
North end between the Delaware River and Assiscunk Creek; East Pearl, Penn, East Union, Barclay crossed by Tatham and Saint Mary; turned, north to the left (-89).

sheet-10.description: The north-east part of Burlington City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the top, between Saint Mary Street on the left and the Assiscunk Creek on the right, from Barclay Street at the top to Jones Avenue at the bottom. East Broad Street crosses the middle of the sheet with the Pennsylvania Railroad drawn in it and a branch curving north-east towards the creek along the right side; an 8 inch water pipe is marked over the bridge. North of East Broad Street stand the Captain James Lawrence School, St. Barnabas Episcopal Church with its Sunday school, rows of frame and brick dwellings, and, on the right, the large Stuart and Peterson Co. stove and hollow ware foundry with enameling, smelting, machine shop and core rooms, and a sand and brick storage shed on the creek bank. South of East Broad Street are the Neidich Process Co. typewriter supplies works (carbon coating and paper stock, ribbon manufacture), St. Paul's R.C. Church and school, a long row of frame dwellings along Earl Street, and a cemetery by the creek with a Boy Scouts' cabin. Clarkson Street and Jones Avenue cross the lower part, with dwellings, a lodge room, a junk dealer and a club house. The streets on the left side of the page continue on sheets 7 and 8. Water pipes and hydrants are lettered throughout.
notes: Street is lettered "Linden (Earl)" south of Clarkson; OpenStreetMap has Linden Avenue there and Earl Street north of Clarkson.
East Broad Street is drawn about 100 feet wide with the railroad in it and was not used as control; its junctions would lie about 8 m off the drawn centre.
Laumaster Street, a short lane off Saint Mary Street, exists today as Laumaster Street in OpenStreetMap; it was not used as control.
Saint Mary to the Assiscunk Creek, Barclay to Jones Av; East Broad with the P.R.R. in it (not used); Stuart and Peterson foundry; Linden (Earl).

sheet-11-1.description: The east side of Burlington City along the Assiscunk Creek, from Jones Avenue at the top of the sheet south past Green Street and Mitchell (Belmont) Street to the State Highway, between St. Mary Street and East Federal Street on the left and the creek on the right. North is towards the top of the sheet. The blocks between St. Mary Street and Linden (Earl) Street are filled with small frame dwellings, mostly of two stories, with a few brick houses along Jones Avenue and an A.M.E. church on St. Mary Street. East of Linden Street lie the William Mersey greenhouses on Jones Avenue, a boat club and more dwellings backing onto the creek. The southern half of the sheet is open ground: the William R. Allen School (coloured) on Mitchell Street, a few dwellings on East Federal Street, and the State Highway crossing the bottom of the sheet with its lots numbered but unbuilt. The Assiscunk Creek runs down the right side of the part. The right-hand portion of the sheet, behind a heavy dividing line, is a separate inset of the Public Service power house and is not part of this area. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in every street. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Linden is labelled 'Linden (Earl)' and Mitchell 'Mitchell (Belmont)', giving the older names; today they are Linden Avenue and Mitchell Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The State Highway is today's Burlington Pike; its junction with East Federal Street lies about 4 to 10 m from the drawn junction and was left out of the control.
Placed from six junctions in the northern two thirds of the part; the State Highway corner at the bottom has no control of its own.
The 'St.' of St. Mary is written out as Saint.

Two parts. Part 1: Jones Av to the State Highway, St Mary to the Assiscunk Creek (Linden = old Earl, Mitchell = old Belmont); State Highway (Burlington Pike) junction displaced, excluded. Part 2 (right of heavy line): inset of the Public Service Corporation Burlington power house and car sheds on the Delaware at the south end of the city.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Public Service Corporation of New Jersey Burlington power house and car sheds, on the Delaware south-west of sheet 16 (no street junction; site rebuilt; needs hand placement against the shore or a feature shared with sheet 16, if one can be found).

sheet-12.description: A rail-and-industry district at the north edge of Burlington City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the top, between the Assiscunk Creek on the left and Logan on the right. East Broad Street and Bordentown Road run up the sheet to the upper right as two parallel streets with a block of frame dwellings between them, crossed near the top right by Corson Street; Columbus Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right, with numbered lots and dwellings on both sides. The Pennsylvania Railroad lines and the Burlington and Mt. Holly branch curve across the sheet, with a freight house and platform at upper left. The industrial buildings include the New Jersey Fence Co. (store house and piles of fence posts), Armour and Co.'s beef store house, W. C. Jones's concrete block factory with a coal yard along the creek, the Burlington Ice and Cold Storage Co. Inc. with its freezing room and laundry, J. F. Smith's greenhouses at the right edge, and at the bottom the H. R. Lindabury and Sons basket factory with its numbered sheds and tool house. East Pearl Street is lettered at the left, near the creek bank, where a heavy line marks the edge of the area drawn on the neighbouring sheet. The compass rose sits at the lower centre; the creek is drawn in blue. Large areas between the tracks are blank.
notes: Columbus Avenue and Corson Street are Columbus Road and Corson Street in OpenStreetMap; Logan is Logan Avenue.
Placed by a two-point helmert (Columbus Road / Logan Avenue and Bordentown Road / Corson Street): low confidence.
Bordentown Road is drawn about 33 feet wide against 59 feet in today's parcels.

Rail yards and works north of Columbus Av (New Jersey Fence Co, ice storage, Lindabury basket factory); East Broad/Bordentown Rd at top right; two-point helmert (Columbus/Logan, Bordentown/Corson), low confidence.

sheet-13.description: A strip of the north end of Burlington City along East Broad Street and Bordentown Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north lies towards the upper left. East Broad Street runs down the left side of the sheet beside a broad bundle of Pennsylvania Railroad tracks, and Bordentown Road runs parallel to it, crossed at the top by Jones Street, in the middle by Hulme Street and at the bottom by Corson Street. The blocks between the two roads hold a few frame dwellings of one and two stories with sheds and outbuildings, a fire engine house (Neptune No. 7 Fire Co.), and, at the top, a row of brick dwellings facing Jones Street. East of Bordentown Road the Stephen Grellet School stands in a block of its own near Jones Street, and a large drawn lot beside the road at the bottom holds a long group of yellow factory sheds belonging to the neighbouring sheet. The right half of the sheet is largely blank except for Columbus Avenue, which crosses the lower right corner on a diagonal, and Hulme Street, which meets it at the right edge; the compass rose stands in a wide empty area. Two blocks beside the tracks are marked as log yards. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are shown in the streets, with fire alarm boxes and hydrants.
notes: The fitted scale is about 2 percent larger than the atlas average.
East Broad Street is drawn about 112 feet wide beside the Pennsylvania Railroad track bundle; its modern line is displaced from the drawn centre.
Columbus Avenue is Columbus Road in OpenStreetMap; it was not used as control.
East Broad St and Bordentown Rd from Jones to Corson, turned -61; scale about 2 percent above atlas; East Broad junctions usable here (rails beside the street).

sheet-14.description: The works of the United States Cast Iron Pipe and Foundry Company at the north end of Burlington City, on the bank of the Delaware River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north lies towards the upper left. The sheet is filled by the company's plant: numbered casting houses with their cleaning sheds and core ovens, a large foundry (No. 4) with cupolas and ovens, a machine shop (No. 5) and pattern shop and storage, a mud house, a cleaning house (No. 27), a sand storage shed, a turbine and dynamo house (No. 6) with a 20 inch water pipe and a stand pipe filled from the river, offices (Nos. 30 and 31), a lumber yard and flask yard, and a long list of the company's fire protection and equipment printed at the lower right. Plant railroad spurs curve through the works and run to the river. East Pearl Street and East Union Street run up the page through and beside the plant, crossed by Thompson Street near the top and Jones Street near the bottom, with rows of frame dwellings of two stories lining East Union Street on its east side. East Broad Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks run down the right edge. The Delaware River forms the left edge of the sheet and the compass rose lies at the upper right.
notes: Placed by a single anchored junction (East Broad Street and Jones Street, from the drawn edge and half the street width) with scale and rotation assumed: low confidence.
East Pearl and East Union Streets here do not match today's OpenStreetMap East Pearl Street, which has been realigned; neither was used as control.
East Broad Street is drawn about 112 feet wide with the railroad in it; its modern line is displaced from the drawn centre.
U.S. Cast Iron Pipe and Foundry Co works on the river between E Pearl, E Union and E Broad; old E Pearl and E Union realigned. Anchored on E Broad / Jones, low confidence.

sheet-15-1.description: The north-east edge of Burlington City where the State Highway leaves Columbus Avenue, the L-shaped main part of sheet 15. It covers the east side of Columbus Avenue from the meeting of Jones Street, Columbus Avenue and the State Highway down to Hulme Street, the wedge of land between Columbus Avenue and the State Highway, and the south side of Hulme Street to the curve of the highway at the right edge. The sheet is turned on the page: Columbus Avenue runs down the left side and Hulme Street across the bottom, with north towards the left. Development is thin and recent: a row of seven pairs of frame dwellings on Columbus Avenue, a few scattered houses and garages inside the wedge, and along Hulme Street a regular row of ten pairs of concrete-block dwellings. The State Highway is drawn 60 feet wide with its lots numbered but mostly vacant, and it curves south to cross Hulme Street near the right edge of the sheet. The left margin repeats the edge of sheet 13 across Columbus Avenue, with Jones Street and Hulme Street lettered there. A pasted correction carries a north arrow and the block number 212. The three boxed areas in the upper right of the sheet are separate parts showing East Broad Street and Bordentown Road. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The State Highway is today's Burlington Pike (US 130), rebuilt as a divided road on a different line here; its junction with Hulme Street was left out of the control.
Placed by a two-point helmert from Columbus Road / Jones Street and Columbus Road / Hulme Street: position, scale and rotation only, low confidence.
The Jones Street junction point is hand-picked at the pixel the detector measured with the State Highway arms.

Four parts. Part 1 (L-shape): Columbus Av, State Highway and Hulme St; State Highway realigned as Burlington Pike, two-point helmert. Part 2 (top middle box): N.J. Fruit Growers' Association warehouse between E. Broad and Bordentown Rd north of the city limits. Part 3 (right box): E. Broad and Bordentown Rd from Jones to Gaunt. Part 4 (middle box): the same roads north of Gaunt, placed by points carried from part 3. Gaunt is a 20 ft paper street, not today's Gauntt Street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: box: New Jersey Fruit Growers' Association warehouse between East Broad Street and Bordentown Road, north of the city limits (no street junction; the two roads run parallel and nothing fixes the position along them; needs a hand-placed position along East Broad Street and Bordentown Road (the warehouse, if it survives)).

sheet-15-3.description: A strip of the north end of Burlington City along East Broad Street and Bordentown Road, from Jones Street at the bottom of the box to the paper street Gaunt at the top, in the boxed right-hand part of sheet 15. The part is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left: East Broad Street runs down its left edge, with the Pennsylvania Railroad noted as lying beyond it, and Bordentown Road down its right side, crossed by Thompson Street and Jones Street. The blocks hold frame dwellings of one and two stories, many with sheds and auto garages, a cooperage, a bakery, a few concrete-block buildings, and a large lot on Jones Street occupied by the Presbyterian Church with its heating furnace. The far side of Bordentown Road is only outlined, and Gaunt Street is drawn as a 20 ft street between dashed lines, continued on the middle box of the same sheet. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B crosses the top right corner. Water pipes run in Thompson, Jones and Bordentown Road. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Gaunt is drawn as a 20 ft paper street about 300 ft north of Thompson; the modern Gauntt Street lies about 650 ft north of Thompson Street, so Gaunt was not used as control.
Placed from four junctions (East Broad Street and Bordentown Road with Thompson Street and Jones Street); no leave-one-out check is possible with four points.
The fitted scale is about 2.5 percent larger than the atlas average.

sheet-15-4.description: A short strip along East Broad Street and Bordentown Road just north of the paper street Gaunt, at the north end of Burlington City, in the middle box of sheet 15. Like the box beside it, it is turned on the page with north towards the upper left: East Broad Street runs down the left side, with the Pennsylvania Railroad noted as lying beyond it, and Bordentown Road down the right. Gaunt is drawn along the bottom as a 20 ft street between dashed lines, continuing the top of the right-hand box. The block between the two roads, numbered 101, is nearly empty: one frame dwelling with a coop, an outbuilding and a few lot lines; the land on both sides is otherwise vacant. Lot depths of 112 and 120 feet are lettered along East Broad Street. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: No surviving junction: placed from three points carried from the right-hand box (sheet-15-3) where both boxes draw the paper street Gaunt, as a helmert; low confidence, and it follows sheet-15-3's placement.
The drawn distance between East Broad and Bordentown Road differs by about 3 percent between this box and the right-hand box.

sheet-16.description: The Thomas Devlin Manufacturing Co. malleable iron works on the Delaware River at the west end of Burlington City, between Reed Street at the top of the sheet and the river shore on the left, with West Pearl Street along the right edge. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Nearly the whole sheet is the one works: a long fire-proof office, storage, manufacturing and blank-storage range along West Pearl Street, the malleable iron foundry with its moulders' rooms and furnaces, two annealing rooms with cast iron floors, grinding and tumbling rooms, core rooms, a pattern vault, pattern and brass pattern shops, an electrical department, a galvanizing room, an engine and dynamo house, sand houses, an acid house, an oil house, an ice house and a pump house drawing from the river. A raised railroad siding and trestle run through the plant between the foundry and the annealing rooms, with another siding beside West Pearl Street. A plank loading wharf, marked not in use and dilapidated, stands on the river shore. Only two dwellings are drawn, on the far side of West Pearl Street; the blocks across Reed Street and West Pearl Street belong to sheet 17 and are left blank. Water pipes, hydrants and an artesian well are marked. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Placed from a single junction (Reed Street / West Pearl Street) with the atlas scale assumed and the rotation from the drawn street lines: low confidence.
North Delaware Avenue, drawn at the top left, has no matching modern street in OpenStreetMap; the works site has been redeveloped.
The plank loading wharf on the river is marked 'not in use' and 'dilap'd'.
Thomas Devlin Mfg Co malleable iron works between Reed St, W. Pearl St and the Delaware; turned like sheet 3. Only junction is Reed / W. Pearl: anchored (scale assumed, rotation from its lines).

sheet-17.description: The west side of Burlington City between the Delaware River and West Broad Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north lies towards the upper left. The river and its blue-tinted bank run down the left edge, with West Delaware Avenue along the shore. West Pearl, Brown, West Union and Conover Streets run down the sheet and are crossed by Wood Street at the top, Tolbot Street, Ellis Street and Reed Street, which closes the lower end. West Broad Street runs down the right edge beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks, with Engle Avenue and Washington Avenue entering from the right. The upper left blocks hold a few large frame dwellings in wide grounds. St. Mary's Hall, a school for girls with chapel, class rooms and school rooms, stands on the river side of West Pearl Street. The dense blocks between West Union Street and West Broad Street are lined with rows of frame and brick dwellings and include the S. Leech Shoe Factory, the Elias Boudinot Public School and a Seventh Day Adventist church. At the upper right a large cemetery surrounds St. Mary's Episcopal church and a chapel. Several blocks near the bottom are largely open, and the lower part of the sheet and the lot at the left edge are bordered by the neighbouring sheets 2, 3, 16 and 18, whose numbers are marked. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches run in most streets.
notes: Tolbot is lettered Tolbot; OpenStreetMap has Talbot Street.
West Delaware Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap under that name.
Conover Street and Brown Street meet Reed Street near the sheet's lower edge; those two junctions were excluded because they carried residuals of 4 to 5 m.
West Pearl to West Broad, Wood to Reed, 100 ft, turned -68 (St. Mary's Hall, cemetery). Conover/Reed and Brown/Reed excluded (4-5 m). Tolbot = Talbot Street.

sheet-18.description: The northwest corner of Burlington City, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points towards the upper left. West Broad Street runs down the left edge beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks, and Wood Street bounds the top. West Federal Street, Juniper Street and Engle Avenue form the built-up blocks at upper left, where small frame dwellings, a few shops and greenhouses stand on narrow lots; Samuel L. Marks's greenhouses occupy a block beside Broad Street and a garage and an M.E. church stand near the top. Washington Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from Broad Street to the State Highway, lined with rows of dwellings and the pink brick works of the Beverly Underwear Company, with a garage at its junction with West Federal Street. Beside the railroad on the left are a vacant factory building, a wood-polishing works and a warehouse. A Drainage Ditch winds down the centre and across the right of the sheet; most of the land to the east of it is open and divided into numbered lots by paper streets (Elder, Willow and Stillbrook Avenues, marked not open), with the State Highway and Lincoln Avenue on the right edge. At the bottom, Moreland, Taylor and Oakland Avenues form a small group of blocks with a few dwellings. Water pipes and block numbers are marked throughout; the compass rose shows the turned orientation.
notes: West Federal is West Federal Street in OpenStreetMap; Moreland is Moorland Avenue today.
Juniper Street meets Engle Avenue as a 40 ft street ending at Engle's north edge; the junction was hand-picked from a full-resolution crop because the detector did not find it.
Broad Street is drawn with the railroad and left out of the control (see the atlas notes on Broad Street).
Washington Avenue is labelled 'Washington Av. or Camden Av.' near the State Highway; the Washington/Camden alternative name is listed under both entries.
NW Burlington, 100 ft, turned (rot -70); W. Broad with railroad at left, Washington (Camden) Av diagonal, Drainage Ditch. One hand-picked point (Engle/Juniper).

sheet-19.description: A residential district of northeastern Burlington City, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with Wood Street along the top edge and Salem Avenue along the bottom, and the State Highway on the left. Mott Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Grant Avenue and Salem Avenue cross Farner, Elm and Fernwood Avenues in a regular grid of numbered blocks. Frame dwellings stand on narrow lots along Lincoln Avenue, Elm Avenue and Farner Avenue and in the blocks at the right, while the upper left and centre are open ground with only a few dwellings. The Samuel Smith Public School occupies the middle of the block bounded by Grant, Farner and Elm Avenues. At lower left the Burlington Silk Company's mill (Brodosilk), with its sawtooth roof, reservoir and fire-hose equipment, stands beside Washington Avenue and Salem Avenue; the sheet carries a detailed key of its water supply and sprinklers. Stillbrook Avenue and Hickory Avenue are drawn as paper streets, and a short stretch of Drainage Ditch runs in at the upper left. The compass rose near the left shows the orientation of the sheet.
notes: Washington Avenue is labelled 'Washington Av. or Camden Av.'; the Washington/Camden alternative name is listed under both entries.
Salem Avenue is Salem Road in OpenStreetMap.
Mott Avenue meets Grant Avenue at two nearby nodes in the modern data; several junctions carry residuals of about 3 m and the part fits at about 2 m RMSE.
NE residential grid (Farner, Elm, Fernwood, Lincoln, Grant, Salem); Burlington Silk Co. mill; 100 ft, rot -89. Farner/Salem rejected (9.7 m).

sheet-20.description: The southern edge of Burlington City where it meets Burlington Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points towards the upper left. A regular grid of numbered blocks (245 to 270) is laid out between Taylor Avenue at the top and Uhler Avenue at the bottom, cut by Park, Chelton and Madison Avenues and by Shady Lane, Woodland, Oakland and Moreland Avenues, with Washington Avenue (or Camden Avenue), 120 feet wide, on the right. Most of the blocks are empty; frame dwellings are built along Moreland Avenue and the east side of the grid near Washington Avenue, and several are marked as streets not open. A drainage ditch with a 25 foot alley beside it runs diagonally across the upper left. At the top left, West Broad Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad pass J. C. Lindsay's foundry. Salem Avenue and the State Highway join Washington Avenue at the upper right. The dash-dot line across the lower part of the sheet is the boundary between the City of Burlington and Burlington Township; below it lie the Odd Fellows' Cemetery with its chapel, a few scattered dwellings, and the River Road and the Burlington Pike at the bottom.
notes: Moreland is Moorland Avenue today; Salem Avenue is Salem Road.
Shady Lane is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used.
Washington Avenue (120 ft) was listed but no junction on it was detected; the fit rests on the grid streets.
The City of Burlington and Burlington Township boundary is drawn as a dash-dot line near the bottom.
South edge grid (Taylor to Uhler, Woodland-Moreland), city/township line, Odd Fellows cemetery; 100 ft, rot -50. Moreland = Moorland Avenue; Washington Av (120 ft) undetected.

sheet-21.description: The middle of Burlington City east of the centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points towards the upper left. High or Main Street runs across the lower part of the sheet from the left edge to Second Street at the right, with shops, a garage, Zion Church and the premises of the Public Service Gas and Electric Company along its north side and dwellings on Ashton Street running south from it. North of High Street the blocks between Wall Street, Gordon Street and Dewey Street are laid out in numbered lots (286 to 296) divided by Tyler, York, Jackson and Lawrence Streets, with an auto house, a gasoline station and a fire company building. East Federal Street crosses the top left with the Public Service Production Company's power house at its junction with Mitchell Street. The land at the right is open and sparsely built: the large blocks 43 and 44, Hurlburt Street and Morris Street, and a garage and a few dwellings near Second Street. Wood Street runs along the bottom with Mott Avenue; State Highway is shown at the top and again at the lower left. Water pipes are marked in nearly every street.
notes: Wetherill and Gordon have no modern match; Hurlburt is Hulbert Street in OpenStreetMap, and Dewey Street, Wall Street and Mitchell Avenue (printed Mitchell St.) survive.
High or Main with Wall, Dewey, Ashton; E. Federal/Mitchell at top; 100 ft, rot -71. Hurlburt = Hulbert Street.

sheet-22.description: The eastern part of Burlington City, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points towards the upper left. High or Main Street crosses the sheet from left to right and is crossed by Second to Ninth Streets, with Chestnut Street and Walnut Street running parallel to it and Wood Street along the lower edge. The numbered blocks (112 to 228 and 314 to 328) are subdivided into narrow lots, but most are unbuilt: frame dwellings stand mainly along High Street and in the blocks at the left, with a cement block works near Second Street and a few buildings on the Walnut and Wood Street edges. Block 218 near the centre is an open square. At the top the numbered streets end at Pope Street and then at an unnamed street at the upper right. Mill Road runs diagonally along the right edge, where the dash-dot line marks the boundary between the City of Burlington and Burlington Township, with Wall Avenue and Central Avenue just beyond. At lower left, Elm Avenue, Fernwood Avenue and Glenwood Avenue run down to Wood Street among large blocks that are not yet built up. Fire alarm boxes and 6-inch water mains are marked along High Street.
notes: In OpenStreetMap the numbered streets are West 2nd to West 8th Street south of High Street and East 2nd to East 7th Street north of it; Martha Street meets Chestnut Street very close to West 6th Street, so Martha was not used.
Mill Road is Mill Road/Mill Street in OpenStreetMap and the Township boundary runs along it.
High or Main with 2nd-9th Streets, Chestnut, Walnut, Wood; 100 ft, rot -71. Chestnut/West 2nd rejected (7.8 m).

sheet-23-1.description: Springside, a village in Burlington Township east of the city, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points towards the upper left; this is the main part of the sheet, outside the heavily outlined inset at the upper left. High or Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet from Mill Road at the left to the five-way junction with Fountain Avenue, Rancocas Avenue and Mt. Holly Avenue near the centre. The City of Burlington and Burlington Township line runs along Mill Road at the left. Below High Street a grid of numbered blocks (330 to 352) is laid out between 11th, 12th and 13th Streets and Cleveland, Wall, Central and Griffith Avenues, with a few dwellings and many empty lots. At the upper right are blocks 353 to 359 along Fountain, Prospect, Bunting and Mt. Holly Avenues and Ellis Boulevard, with dwellings on narrow lots, the Springside Baptist Chapel on Mt. Holly Avenue and the Independent Fire Co. house on Chapel Street. Block 323 between Mill Road and Fountain Avenue north of High Street holds a few scattered dwellings and garages. Wall Avenue and 14th, 15th and 16th Streets lead off to the lower right, where one street is lettered '(not named)'. Ellis Boulevard and Dresser Street continue on the inset at the upper left, marked by the sheet number 23 at the right edge.
notes: Mt. Holly Avenue is lettered in a way that reads like 'Mi Holly Av.' (the index prints 'Mt. Holly Ave.'); today it is Mount Holly Road. Dresser Street is Dresser Avenue, Ellis Boulevard is Ellis Avenue.
The heavily outlined area at the upper left is a separate inset (part 2) continuing Mt. Holly Avenue, Ellis Boulevard and Dresser Street east of the right edge.
The fit uses 11 junctions along High Street, 11th to 13th Streets, Cleveland and Wall Avenues and Fountain Avenue; the area north and east of Fountain Avenue has control only along Fountain Avenue.

Springside, 100 ft, rot -71. Two parts: part 1 main sheet (High, 11th-16th, Cleveland, Wall, Fountain, Prospect, Bunting, Rancocas); part 2 heavily outlined inset at upper left (Mt. Holly Av, Ellis Blvd, Dresser St, Springside Public School) continuing east of the right edge; two-point helmert, low confidence.

sheet-23-2.description: An inset in the heavily outlined upper-left corner of sheet 23, continuing Springside east of the main part of the sheet: Mt. Holly Avenue from Ellis Boulevard eastward, and Dresser Street running from Mt. Holly Avenue down to Rancocas Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned like the rest of the sheet, with north towards the upper left. The Springside Public School, a heated and electrically lighted building, stands on the south side of Mt. Holly Avenue in the large block 355, which is otherwise open. Narrow lots numbered 101 to 123 line Mt. Holly Avenue, with a handful of frame dwellings on both sides, and a few dwellings and auto garages stand along Dresser Street and in block 354 west of it. Block 356 lies north of Mt. Holly Avenue. The inset is bounded by a heavy line on its right and bottom; the sheet number 23 inside it and at the right edge of the main part marks where the two join.
notes: Placed by a two-point helmert from Dresser Avenue / Mount Holly Road and Dresser Avenue / Rancocas Road (today's names); the Ellis Avenue junction, only 30 m away, was left out. Low confidence.
Mt. Holly Avenue is lettered in a way that reads like 'Mi Holly Av.'; today it is Mount Holly Road. Ellis Boulevard is Ellis Avenue and Dresser is Dresser Avenue.
